correctness.rationale: The alternating determinant bracket makes the Reynolds defect alternating and trilinear, so one basis triple suffices. The resulting identity is det(R)e1=(sigma2(R)-det(R))R(e1), from which the three structural alternatives follow by an exhaustive split on R(e1). The finite-field total is obtained by disjoint case counts; the difficult middle case is reduced to det=sigma2=0 and counted by trace fibers and fixed-line preservation. Rank one is automatic, rank three is counted through B-I in SL2, and rank two follows by subtraction. Exhaustive F2 and F3 replay agrees exactly.

value.rationale: The three-dimensional algebra [e1,e2,e3]=e1 is the canonical finite-dimensional example already singled out in the primary paper. The result turns the newly introduced four-term Reynolds identity into a single characteristic-free matrix criterion and completely resolves all finite-field rank strata. The exact invertible count also sharpens the source's qualitative derivation correspondence, while the singular strata show that the full Reynolds locus is substantially larger than the invertible theory.
